newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Erupting volcano burns forests in war-torn Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Erupting volcano burns forests in war-torn Zaire.

text.p: Eastern Zaire's Nyamulagira volcano erupted on Sunday close to camps abandoned by Rwandan Hutu refugees, spewing jets of lava high into the air and forming a lava trail 10 km (six miles) long through forests.

A Reuters correspondent who travelled to Rumangabe, north of the deserted refugee camps of Kahindo and Katale, saw about 10 km of burning forest in the Virunga national park left by boiling lava as it moved northwestwards.
Kahindo and Katale were home to thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees but they fled six weeks ago ahead of a military advance by Rwandan-backed Zairean rebels who now control much of eastern Zaire.
The rebels have captured the eastern Zairean towns of Uvira, Kamanyola, Bukavu and Goma and there is reported fighting around the town of Beni north of Goma.
The refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 after civil war and genocidal killings in which many of them took part.
A U.N. refugee agency spokesman in the Rwandan capital Kigali told Reuters the eruption posed no threat to the human population as the area was abandoned weeks ago.
"It probably does not pose any hazard to people. We checked and the Katale and Kahindo camps are completely empty," said UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg.
The crater of the volcano was hidden by thick cloud.
The slopes of the volcano and surrounding areas are home to tropical rain forest and rare mountain gorillas.
The volcano, 40 km (25 miles) northwest of the Zairean border town of Goma, is one of seven in the area of the Virunga National Park as well as on the Rwanda-Zaire-Uganda border.
Only two are active, Nyamulagira and Nyaragongo.
Apart from refugees, the nearest centre of habitation are villages 10 km (six miles) away.
While Nyaragongo is a so-called "soft-lava" volcano, with a tube of lava which moves up and down inside its core, Nyamulagira is considered a potentially explosive volcano.
If the lava spout continues to erupt, it is considered likely the whole volcano itself could blow.
The last time Nyamulagira erupted was in July 1994 when a crack opened on a slope facing Virunga National Park and hot lava flowed into the park for days.
Usually Nyamulagira erupts every two years, experts say.
Nyamulagira's sister, Nyaragongo, was also active in 1994, when a lava lake in its crater reappeared, causing an eerie orange light to shine on to clouds at night.
Since then lava inside the crater has been moving up and down, experts say.
In 1977, enormous cracks appeared in Nyaragongo's side and more than 60 million cubic metres of lava poured out of the volcano's cone both to the north and south.
The lava covered a distance of 10 km in barely 20 minutes, stopping short of Goma city but coming within several hundred metres of Goma airport. Seventy deaths were reported, U.N. officials say.
